title: Capital Credit Payout and Offset Standards by Patron Class
content:
# Payout and Offset Standards by Patron Class

**Product:** Capital Credits (Patronage Capital). The figures below govern how retired capital credits owed to a member are paid out in each patron class.

| Patron class | How an active member is paid | How an inactive member or an estate is paid | Smallest payout by check | Smallest payout by bill credit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Residential Patron Class | bill credit | check | $10.00 | $1.00 |
| Seasonal Patron Class | bill credit | check | $10.00 | $1.00 |
| Farm Patron Class | bill credit | check | $10.00 | $1.00 |
| General Service Patron Class | bill credit | check | $10.00 | $1.00 |
| Irrigation Patron Class | bill credit | check | $10.00 | $1.00 |
| Large Power Patron Class | check | check | $25.00 | $1.00 |

| Term common to every class | Value |
|---|---|
| Payable below the smallest payout carried forward and added to the next payout | Yes |
| Retirements first applied to the member's unpaid final-billed balances | Yes |
| Order of offset | oldest final balance first |

## Distinguishing the classes

- The Large Power Patron Class pays active members by check rather than bill credit, and its smallest check is $25.00 instead of $10.00.
- In every class an inactive member and an estate are paid by check.
- The $1.00 bill-credit minimum is the same in all six classes.

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A check remainder of $9.99 in the Residential Patron Class is below $10.00 and stays payable for the next payout; a remainder of exactly $10.00 is paid.
- A check remainder of $24.99 in the Large Power Patron Class is below $25.00 and is carried forward; $25.00 is paid.
- A bill-credit remainder of $0.99 in the Farm Patron Class is carried forward; $1.00 is posted.
